name: Ukraine
who: Russia vs Ukraine, with the US mediating talks
what: Full-scale invasion, now a grinding war of attrition
when: Started Feb 24, 2022 — day 1,650+ and still going
how: Daily drone, missile and artillery strikes along a front over 1,100 km long
current: Russia and Ukraine are engaged in intense fighting, with Russia reviving demands that NATO retrench to secure a Ukraine deal. Ukrainian drones have attacked Russian targets, including the Crimean Bridge, while Russia has launched missile strikes on Kyiv, causing power outages. The US has floated the idea of Ukraine ceding Donbas for NATO membership, but Ukraine's leader has rejected this proposal.

sources.label: The New York Times: Russia Revives Demand That NATO Retrench to Secure Ukraine Deal
BBC: Komyshuvakha: Ukraine accuses Russia of targeting rescue operation after strikes that killed 57
The Guardian: Russian attacks have left Kyiv with devastating power outages

perspective.dominant_frame: Western sources, such as The New York Times and The Guardian, frame the conflict as a war between Russia and Ukraine, with a focus on Russian aggression and Ukrainian resistance. Regional specialists, such as the BBC, also report on the conflict, highlighting the humanitarian impact of the war.

name: Gaza
what: War technically under ceasefire, but violence continues
when: War since Oct 7, 2023; ceasefire since Oct 10, 2025
how: Over 1,300 people killed since the "ceasefire" began; disarmament and reconstruction stalled
current: Israeli forces have killed six people across the Gaza Strip, including a six-year-old boy, according to Gaza officials and hospitals. The death toll from the Israeli war in Gaza has surged to 74,653 civilians killed since October 7, 2023. An additional 176,007 Palestinians have been injured in the past three years.

sources.label: Arab News: Gaza officials say Israeli forces killed 6 in Gaza, including child
AP News: Israeli strike on a Gaza hospital kills 6 people, health authorities say
Al Jazeera: Israeli strikes hit medical complex as nine killed across Gaza

perspective.dominant_frame: The conflict in Gaza is framed as a war with high casualties and ongoing violence, with both Tier 1 and Tier 3 sources reporting on the latest incidents and death toll. Tier 1 sources such as AP News and Arab News focus on the factual reporting of the events, while Tier 3 sources like Al Jazeera provide more context and perspective on the conflict.

name: Iran
who: Israel and the US vs Iran
what: A leadership-shattering war, now in an uneasy pause
how: US-Israeli strikes killed Iran’s Supreme Leader; his son succeeded him; Hormuz still shut
current: Iran has expanded its attacks in the Gulf, striking a U.S. air base in Kuwait and repeatedly targeting a radar facility in Bahrain, in retaliation for a U.S. strike on an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island. The fighting follows stalled mediation talks and a hardening of Iran’s position after recent U.S. political developments.

sources.label: AP News: Iran fires on a US air base in Kuwait after US strikes
AP News: Iranian drone attack targets US radar facility in Bahrain
BBC: Kuwait says it repelled first Iranian attack in two months after US strikes island
The Jerusalem Post: Emboldened by US midterm results, Iran drafts plans to escalate war

perspective.dominant_frame: Tier‑1 outlets (AP, BBC) describe the recent strikes as a direct tit‑for‑tat response by Iran to the U.S. attack on Qeshm Island, emphasizing the widening geographic scope to Kuwait and Bahrain. Tier‑3 coverage (Jerusalem Post) adds that Iran’s hardening stance is linked to perceived U.S. political weakness after the midterm elections, highlighting a political motive beyond the immediate retaliation.

escalation.note: Iran’s attacks on Kuwait and Bahrain after the U.S. strike keep the conflict at the same high‑escalation level.

name: Sudan
who: Army (SAF) vs the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces
what: Civil war hardening into a formal partition
when: Since April 15, 2023, now in its 4th year
how: RSF controls Darfur and the west; army holds the center, north and east
current: A Sudanese army airstrike in West Kordofan killed at least 13 civilians, including women and children, while UN data show drones have caused over 1,000 civilian deaths this year, accounting for three‑quarters of war‑related fatalities. Tensions with Ethiopia have risen as both governments accuse each other of backing armed groups, and the humanitarian situation remains dire, with aid agencies warning of a deepening hunger crisis.

Reuters: Drones account for nearly three‑quarters of Sudan war deaths this year

name: Myanmar
